Subject: EU-only processing requirement + Schrems II evidence request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. As part of HealthCorp's procurement checklist we need to confirm that any customer data linked to EU residents is processed and stored only within EU jurisdictions (no outbound transfers to third countries). Per Schrems II review we also need to collect evidence supporting our legal basis for transfers (SCCs) and technical controls. Could you provide the following:

- Explicit confirmation of EU-only processing for processing and backups (including region names).
- Copy of standard SCCs or rider language you propose.
- Details on KMS/master key residency and whether keys are customer-managed.
- Evidence of deletion/purge procedures including backup retention and cross-region failover behavior.
- List of subprocessors and whether any have potential access from non-EU operators.

We'd like to include the above in our security appendix and need initial responses by EOD Tuesday to keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Emma Turner
Head of Security & Privacy
HealthCorp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EU-only processing requirement + Schrems II evidence request

Emma — thanks, and appreciated the timeline. High-level answers below and I'll follow up with an internal thread to pull the artifacts you requested.

- EU-only processing: Yes. For your account we can enforce in-region processing and storage confined to EU cloud regions (Frankfurt, Amsterdam). No data leaves those regions for processing or backups unless a customer explicitly enables cross-region failover.
- SCCs: We use the latest EU standard contractual clauses; our legal team can provide a redline-friendly copy and a short rider used for EU-only processing commitments.
- KMS: Customer keys can be BYOK via partner KMS in EU. Default keys are region-bound and managed with strict access controls.
- Deletion: We support immediate object deletion and a documented certified purge workflow; backups are retained for 30 days by default in-region and can be configured per-contract.
- Subprocessors: Full current list attached; we provide notice and attestations for subprocessor access controls.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal pull: loop in Hannah (security) for operational evidence and Marissa for contract language.
2) Deliver a single zip with: SCCs copy, region diagram, KMS short whitepaper, deletion log example, subprocessor attestation.
3) Confirm timeline — can we target COB Tue for the artifact bundle?

I'll follow up internally now.

Cheers,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan/Marissa — we have the artifacts; attaching: inregion_kms_policy.pdf (short KMS residency + BYOK steps), backup-evidence-log.csv (sanitized example showing EU-only backups), and a one-page deletion attestation template we use for customers. Notes below:

- Region enforcement: Our control plane supports tenant-scoped region pinning. For Dedicated/Private customers we enforce routing such that compute and storage remain in the pinned EU regions. Hosted customers get account-level region constraints and we provide periodic verification logs.
- Backups & failover: Backups are stored in the same region by default. Cross-region replication is opt-in and will not be enabled without contractual permission. For DR tests we can perform a scoped replication inside EU regions only.
- KMS: BYOK with customer-managed KMS in EU is supported; keys never leave the EU and HSM-backed keys can be used for higher assurance.
- SCCs: Legal provides standard SCCs but operational evidence (logs, snapshots) is provided as attestation rather than appended into the clauses.

I'll assemble the zip and mark sensitive fields sanitized. ETA to Jordan: EOD Mon for the package so we meet HealthCorp's Tue deadline.

—Hannah
